How many simulations does an ABC posterior rest on?

Source: R/abc.R
abc_diagnose.Rd

The posterior of abc_fit() for an observation is a weighted sample of the reference table, with weights from each random forest. For each observation and parameter this gives the effective sample size of the weights (Kish) and the Pareto k-hat of their upper tail (Vehtari et al. 2024), computed by posterior::pareto_khat() on the positive weights, and for each observation the statistics that fall outside the central coverage of the reference table.

Usage

abc_diagnose(fit, newdata, coverage = 0.99)

Arguments

fit

An mc_abc_fit.

newdata

Named numeric vector of observed statistics or a data frame with one observation per row.

coverage

Central probability of the reference table within which a statistic counts as inside.

Value

A data frame with observation, parameter, n_positive (simulations with positive weight), ess, khat, khat_threshold, n_outside (statistics of the observation outside the central coverage of the table) and outside (their names).

Details

The weights of random forests are not importance ratios, so the thresholds of k-hat, derived for importance sampling, do not carry over. In our checks (data-raw/abc_diagnose.R), k-hat and the effective sample size did not predict which estimates were wrong within the model, while data from another model had about half the effective sample size and more statistics outside the table. Read them as warnings that the observation is unlike the simulations, not as measures of the precision of an estimate. An observation outside the range of the simulated statistics is the clearer warning, since the forests then extrapolate from the edge of the table without saying so.

References

Vehtari, A., Simpson, D., Gelman, A., Yao, Y., & Gabry, J. (2024). Pareto smoothed importance sampling. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 25(72), 1–58.

See also

Other inference: abc_choose(), abc_cv(), abc_fit(), abc_ppc(), abc_recovery(), abc_table(), fold_summarise(), observe_detection(), spatial_folds()

Examples

set.seed(1)
table <- data.frame(a = runif(500))
table$s1 <- table$a + rnorm(500, 0, 0.05)
fit <- abc_fit(table, "a", "s1", ntree = 100)
abc_diagnose(fit, data.frame(s1 = c(0.5, 3)))
#> Warning: Number of tail draws cannot be less than 5. Changing to 5.
#> Warning: Number of tail draws cannot be less than 5. Changing to 5.
#>   observation parameter n_positive      ess khat khat_threshold n_outside
#> 1           1         a         13 5.532480   NA             NA         0
#> 2           2         a         11 4.602561   NA             NA         1
#>   outside
#> 1        
#> 2      s1
